items.title: Why the Hell Did Trump’s Golfing Buddy Get a $500,000 Payout from the IRS?
items.content: It seems that the principle of kicking the ball out onto the fairway has many applications beyond the golf course.

items.title: Zohran Mamdani Is Making the Right Decision to Close Rikers Island
items.content: I don’t care what detractors might say. That place is where inmates—and the Eighth Amendment—go to die horrible deaths, and it deserves to be shut down.

items.title: Putin and Xi Just Made Trump Look Like an Absolute Sucker
items.content: Agreeing to a “peace declaration” with a couple of authoritarian nutjobs is certainly a choice.

items.title: Of Course Trump’s Judicial Nominees Are a Bunch of Election-Denying Yahoos
items.content: At a Senate Judiciary Committee hearing on Wednesday, seven fools who could soon have federal seats refused to admit that Joe Biden won in 2020. Yikes.

items.title: A West Virginia County Could Soon Become a Nuclear-Waste Dump Against Its Will
items.content: The state’s energy office decided not to consult with residents, which is just stellar governing all around.

items.title: An Army Facility in Iowa Plans to Detonate Toxic Materials, Which Is Just Great News for the People and Animals Who Live Nearby
items.content: The explosion will apparently create a “dust plume containing lead.” Nice.

items.title: Meet the Trump-Simping U.S. Attorney Who’s Going to Try His Darnedest to Protect the President from Democratic Oversight
items.content: Aaron Reitz has spent the past few weeks firing off letters to various Democratic legislators threatening all kinds of legal thunder and lightning.

items.title: As More Wins for Democrats Roll In, We Must Remind Ourselves That the Fight Is Still Ahead
items.content: Alaska was finally called for Mary Peltola. I sure hope Hakeem Jeffries, the soon-to-be Speaker of the House, knows what to do with his majority.

items.title: To No One’s Surprise, Trump’s Handpicked Navy Secretary Is Just as Incompetent and Heartless as He Is
items.content: Hung Cao’s confirmation hearing went just about as badly as any I’ve ever seen.

items.title: The Supreme Court Has Finally Decided to Do Something About Trump’s War on DEI
items.content: All it took was a drastic midterm swing to get the carefully crafted conservative majority to quit going along with everything the president wants.

items.title: The Highly Classified NSA Comms Network Is Down, but Don’t Worry! Trump Says “It’s Fine.”
items.content: Thanks, Mr. President, I’m totally reassured.

items.title: Leaked Bank Documents Have Just Revealed the Staggering Extent of Epstein’s Shady Finances
items.content: You’ll never guess whose name also came up.

items.title: Of Course the FAA Uses Technology That Average Americans Abandoned Probably 20 Years Ago
items.content: This is all Ronald Reagan’s fault, I just know it.

items.title: Turns Out Chuck Schumer’s Bid for Senate Majority Leader Isn’t as Done a Deal as We Thought
items.content: The newly elected senators are looking toward someone else entirely—and history might be on their side.

items.title: Sean Duffy Is a Perfect Reality-TV Politician. Too Bad for America.
items.content: As a fellow MTV veteran, I recognize that the transportation secretary has been practicing for this moment since his days.

items.title: The FAA Ground Stop, Like Many of the Trump Administration’s Problems, Is Somehow Joe Biden’s Fault
items.content: Give these buffoons enough time and they’ll cast blame on every Democratic president back to Grover Cleveland.

items.title: Somehow It Makes Perfect Sense That What Jensen Huang Inspires in Trump Is ... Empathy
items.content: On the one hand, it’s empathy for a philanderer who may have compromised national security. On the other hand, between this and the interview, displaying real human emotion twice in one week might be a new record.

items.title: Jensen Huang’s Shoes Were the Tell
items.content: I like men’s shoes and I’ve sold men’s shoes. A man’s footwear reveals facets of his public persona—and his private desires.

items.title: The Blue Tsunami Made Waves in Ways I Didn’t Expect, but I’m More Than Glad to See It
items.content: Sure, some elections touched upon the second-worst idea in American politics. But we have to take the wins when we can.

items.title: I Can Feel the Tremors of History Rumbling Beneath Scott Colom’s Victory
items.content: The senator-elect from Mississippi invoked Medger Evers in his winning speech, which reminded me of how far we’ve come—and how far we still have to go.

items.title: The White House to Rep. Robert Garcia: “Please Stop Picking On the President!”
items.content: In a hilariously worded letter, Trump’s counsel claims that the incoming House oversight-committee chair has been making “abusive” threats. Okay then.

items.title: Happy Holidays! The Trump Administration Is Cutting Food-Assistance Programs Again!
items.content: The GOP loses spectacularly, then immediately decides to do as much damage as possible before the Democrats take over. Why am I not surprised?

items.title: I Guess We’re Going Have to Deal with Pete Hegseth for Another Two Months
items.content: The House vote to impeach the Secretary of Talking About War failed yesterday, partially because Democratic members were stuck in traffic and missed it. Great work by all.
